items.q: Minimum illness duration for schizophrenia in DSM pattern (including prodrome and residual) is what?
items.exp: DSM requires six months of disturbance with at least one month of active phase symptoms (or less if treated). One month alone fits brief or schizophreniform categories by duration.
r: Incorrect. One month active phase sits inside longer course.
Correct. Six months total disturbance.
Incorrect. Two years was older chronicity notions.
Incorrect. Two weeks is too brief for any primary psychosis label.

items.q: After failure of two adequate antipsychotic trials, the indicated drug is what?
items.exp: Treatment resistant schizophrenia (two adequate trials) mandates clozapine offer with haematological monitoring; delay worsens outcomes. ECT augments clozapine resistance later in specialist care.
r: Incorrect. Rotating similar D2 blockers repeats failure.
Correct. Clozapine for treatment resistance.
Incorrect. Lithium treats mania, not resistant psychosis core.
Incorrect. ECT is adjunct after clozapine pathways.
items.kp: Two strikes and clozapine comes in.

items.q: All currently effective antipsychotics share which core pharmacology?
o: Dopamine D2 receptor blockade or partial agonism
items.exp: D2 antagonism (or partial agonism at D2) is the common antipsychotic mechanism correlating with positive symptom control; atypicality adds serotonergic and other actions modifying side effects.
r: Incorrect. That is antidepressant action.
Correct. D2 blockade or partial agonism.
Incorrect. NMDA agonism is pro psychotic direction research.
Incorrect. GABA drugs sedate and treat anxiety or seizures.

items.q: Which feature most separates schizophrenia from delusional disorder?
o: Prominent hallucinations, disorganisation or negative symptoms with functional decline
items.exp: Delusional disorder keeps encapsulated delusions with otherwise preserved function and minimal hallucinations; schizophrenia adds broader psychopathology and marked functional deterioration.
r: Incorrect. Both share delusions.
Correct. Breadth of symptoms plus decline defines schizophrenia.
Incorrect. Age overlaps both diagnoses.
Incorrect. Persecution occurs in both.
items.kp: One encapsulated belief versus whole mind illness.

items.q: Clozapine requires blood monitoring primarily because of which risk?
items.exp: Clozapine can cause severe neutropenia and agranulocytosis (about 1 percent spectrum), mandating scheduled full blood counts with stop rules, plus vigilance for myocarditis and severe constipation.
r: Correct. Neutropenia monitoring is mandatory.
Incorrect. Platelet excess is not the monitored danger.
Incorrect. Haemolysis is not clozapine signature.
Incorrect. Red cell excess is unrelated.

items.q: Prodromal schizophrenia most typically shows what presentation?
o: Social withdrawal, declining function and attenuated psychotic symptoms in adolescence
items.exp: Attenuated psychosis syndrome with withdrawal, school decline, suspicion and perceptual oddities precedes frank psychosis in many, though most prodromal clinic attendees do not convert, requiring careful non stigmatising follow up.
r: Incorrect. Mania is mood episode presentation.
Correct. Withdrawal plus attenuated symptoms in youth.
Incorrect. Dementia is late life cognitive disease.
Incorrect. Panic alone lacks attenuated psychosis.

items.q: Lifetime suicide mortality in schizophrenia is approximately what and peaks when?
o: About 5 percent, early illness and post discharge
items.exp: Around 5 percent die by suicide, risk highest early in illness, after discharge and with depressive symptoms, insight and prior attempts. Vigilance in early psychosis services targets this window.
r: Incorrect. Risk is substantial, not negligible.
Correct. About 5 percent, early peak.
Incorrect. Half is far too high.
Incorrect. Risk clusters early, not evenly.
items.kp: Early psychosis carries the suicide peak.

items.q: Long acting injectable antipsychotics principally solve which problem?
o: Covert nonadherence and relapse from missed doses
items.exp: Depot formulations make adherence transparent and steady levels, cutting relapse and hospitalisation where missed oral doses drive recurrence. They do not change drug efficacy molecule itself.
r: Incorrect. Resistance needs clozapine pathway.
Correct. Adherence transparency and relapse prevention.
Incorrect. Negative symptoms persist despite route.
Incorrect. Movement risks remain drug dependent.
items.kp: Depots expose missed doses, they do not add potency.

items.q: Cannabis use in adolescence interacts with schizophrenia risk how?
o: Increases risk, especially high potency daily use and genetic vulnerability
items.exp: Daily high potency cannabis in adolescence multiplies psychosis risk several fold in vulnerable individuals and advances onset; cessation advice is core early psychosis care. Association shows dose response and temporality.
r: Incorrect. Evidence points opposite.
Correct. Dose dependent risk increase in vulnerable youth.
Incorrect. Replicated association exists.
Incorrect. Lasting risk beyond intoxication is demonstrated.
items.kp: Strong daily cannabis in teens feeds psychosis risk.

items.q: Catatonia in schizophrenia spectrum (and mood disorders) first line treatment is what?
o: Benzodiazepine (lorazepam) challenge then ECT if needed
items.exp: Catatonia (stupor, waxy flexibility, negativism, posturing) responds to lorazepam challenge in most, with ECT definitive for refractory or malignant forms. Antipsychotics can worsen catatonia and trigger neuroleptic malignant overlap.
r: Incorrect. Antipsychotics may worsen catatonia.
Correct. Lorazepam first, ECT if refractory.
Incorrect. Antidepressants do not unlock catatonia.
Incorrect. Restraint is safety last resort, not treatment.
items.kp: Frozen patient: lorazepam melts, ECT rescues.
